spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The root count is protected by two adaptive recoveries: enlarge the negative interval when roots may lie outside it, and increase precision when a sudden count collapse signals corrupted Sturm signs. An explicitly reconstructed complex zero is retained as a cross-check, not confused with the primary counting certificate.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using the stated fact that the real zeros are negative, the computation counts on intervals ending at zero, initially reuses a known interval, and decreases the left endpoint when too few real roots are counted without finding a complex zero. The source reports that abrupt implausible count drops were restored to the expected degree-dependent pattern by raising precision; it also treats a complex zero obtained from a local extremum as an extra check.
directed.conceptual_reading: Interval adequacy and arithmetic adequacy are distinct failure modes, so the algorithm diagnoses and repairs them separately. The expected neighboring-degree count pattern acts as a falsifier, while the explicit complex root supplies an independent representation of the same obstruction.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Negativity restricts the search to a half-line; adaptive finite intervals bridge that half-line to endpoint Sturm counts. Precision escalation repairs unreliable sign data, and Newton reconstruction bridges the root-count deficit to a visible conjugate pair.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Coverage depends on the stated negativity result and on actually enlarging the interval enough. Restoring an expected pattern and finding a Newton root are corroborating diagnostics, not standalone replacements for trustworthy coefficient errors and Sturm signs; the source presents this as a practical strategy rather than a complete reproduced formal certificate.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the adaptive strategy and hierarchy of checks; exact numerical reliability still depends on high-precision evaluation and external facts not proved in this unit.
